choices.text: The student is right - the two words name one event
Pollination is delivery: the male gamete must still fuse with the ovule for fertilisation.
Fertilisation is delivery and pollination is fusion
Neither event is needed to make a seed

questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Pollination is fertilisation. Reteach point: Pollination is delivery: the male gamete must still fuse with the ovule for fertilisation.
questions.prompt: A student says pollination and fertilisation are the same thing. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: Pollination only delivers pollen to the stigma; if the male gamete never fuses with the ovule, fertilisation has not happened.
questions.feedback: A strong answer separates delivery from fusion: landing is not joining.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why a flower can be pollinated but not fertilised.

choices.text: On the stigma, as pollen lands
Inside the ovule, when the gametes fuse
In the air, while pollen travels

questions.feedback: Fertilisation is fusion, and fusion happens inside the ovule - not during the journey or on landing.

questions.answer: Any two of: wind lifts it, water carries it, animals drop it, or a pod explodes and scatters it. Dispersal moves seeds away from the parent so young plants compete less for light, water and space.
questions.feedback: Credit any two carriers from scene 3 plus the competition reason.
questions.prompt: Name two ways a seed can be dispersed and say why dispersal helps the plant.
